AT.name: Duftendes Mariengras
AT.citation: Shared German-language name confirmed native in Germany (Bavarian State Office for the Environment); no Austria-specific variant found, shared DACH-region vocabulary

CA.name: Sweetgrass
CA.citation: Widely documented sacred plant among Indigenous peoples in Canada; Wikipedia, Native Plant Trust

CA.name: Foin d'odeur
CA.citation: The Canadian Encyclopedia; genuine French-Canadian usage confirmed by native-plant nursery Pepiniere Nordique (Quebec)

CH.name: Duftendes Mariengras
CH.citation: Wikipedia notes continental European range extends north from Switzerland (i.e. CH is near the range's southern edge); shared German-language name, no Switzerland-specific variant found

CN.name: 茅香
CN.citation: Historical Chinese materia medica (Zhenglei Bencao, Bencao Pinhui Jingyao) and modern TCM reference (baicao99.com) confirm this species-specific identification. Explicitly distinct from the modern term 香茅 (Xiangmao, different character order), which denotes lemongrass (Cymbopogon) - a real character-order confusion trap

CZ.name: Tomkovice vonná
CZ.citation: herbar.webnode.cz and adaptogeny.cz explicitly distinguish tomkovice vonna (genus Hierochloe, this species) from tomka vonna (genus Anthoxanthum, a different species - Anthoxanthum odoratum, sweet vernal grass). A live example of exactly the cross-species confusion flagged for this plant

DE.name: Duftendes Mariengras
DE.citation: Bavarian State Office for the Environment (LfU Bayern); genuinely native, critically endangered, ~90% population decline documented. German Wikipedia

DK.name: Festgræs
DK.citation: Danish Wikipedia; Naturbasen.dk, genuinely native though rare, found on damp meadows with calcareous soil

FI.name: Lännenmaarianheinä
FI.citation: Suomen Lajitietokeskus (Finnish Biodiversity Information Facility); Finnish Wikipedia. Correctly distinguished from three sibling species in genus Hierochloe (australis, hirta, alpina), each with distinct Finnish names in the same taxonomic system

FR.name: Foin d'odeur
FR.citation: Genuine wild presence confirmed, protected species in the Southern Alps (jardinage.pagesjaunes.fr); French Wikipedia

GB.name: Holy grass
GB.citation: Wikipedia, explicitly documented as the UK-specific English name (distinct from 'sweet grass' used elsewhere); recorded in four Scottish counties and one in north-eastern England

IE.name: Holy grass
IE.citation: Wikipedia confirms exactly one recorded site in Ireland - genuine but extremely marginal presence; shares the same English name as GB usage

JP.name: コウボウ
JP.citation: Kotobank encyclopedia (citing botanist Makino Tomitaro's etymology linking it to Chinese Maoxiang); Kyoto Prefecture Red Data Book (government conservation document, listed as critically endangered); Hiroshima University Digital Museum

KR.name: 향모
KR.citation: Genuinely native to Korea (treeinfo.net); Korean Wikipedia genus article, distinguished from the related sanhyangmo (Hierochloe alpina)

NL.name: Veenreukgras
NL.citation: Dutch Ministry of Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality protected species database (minlnv.nederlandsesoorten.nl); Dutch national Red List; genuinely native, found mainly in North/South Holland and Utrecht

NO.name: Marigras
NO.citation: Artsdatabanken (Norwegian Biodiversity Information Centre, government agency); genuinely common across most of Norway

PL.name: Turowka wonna
PL.citation: atlas-roslin.pl, a serious Polish botanical database documenting the species official protected status (included in statutory protection since 1957). Preferred over the colloquial zubrowka, which properly denotes either the plant informally or the vodka brand

RU.name: Зубровка душистая
RU.citation: Russian Wikipedia (formal botanical citation: Gubanov et al., Illustrated Key to Plants of Central Russia); Plantarium.ru

SE.name: Doftmyskgräs
SE.citation: Swedish Wikipedia, genuinely reproducing/native in Sweden; Swedish Botanical Society (botanikportalen.se)

SK.name: Tomkovica vonná
SK.citation: Multiple independent Slovak nursery/retail sources; critically endangered species in Slovakia. Follows the same genus-distinct naming pattern as Czech (tomkovica = Hierochloe, tomka = Anthoxanthum)

UA.name: Чаполоч пахуча
UA.citation: Ukrainian Wikipedia; Ukrainian Pharmaceutical Encyclopedia; genuinely native across Polissya and forest-steppe regions

US.name: Sweetgrass
US.citation: One of the four sacred medicines for many Indigenous peoples in the United States; Wikipedia, Native Plant Trust. Distinct from Anthoxanthum odoratum (sweet vernal grass, unrelated) and from buffalo grass (Bouteloua dactyloides / Stenotaphrum secundatum, also unrelated)
